summary: In a small computer model rather than human testing, Glasdegib received a high score for liver issues and a low score for heart issues [M]. The drug carries the strongest FDA warning because it can cause severe birth defects or death in an unborn baby [3]. Patients are also warned against donating blood during treatment and for at least 30 days after, and their hearts should be monitored for an irregular electrical pattern known as QTc prolongation [3]. Additionally, one clinical study involving the drug was stopped early due to side effects [6].
